query: Can I use my excess Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions to offset my outstanding MediSave payable?
reference_answer: CAYE contributions in excess of your MediSave payable for the year will be automatically used to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years, if any1. Any excess thereafter will be refunded to your bank account.You can also choose to boost your healthcare savings by retaining the excess CAYE contributions in your MediSave Account to earn up to 5% interest per annum, and to offset future MediSave payable. To do so, please apply via theSelf-employment dashboardusing your Singpass.1This will take effect for CAYE contributions made from 2023. Pleasewrite to usif you do not wish to use your CAYE contributions to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years.

The MediSave payable is based on your annual net trade income (NTI) derived as a self-employed person and not the number of licences. If you have a total yearly NTI of more than $6,000 from your licence(s), you are required to make contributions to your MediSave Account.

Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rates may change when you (i) update your CAYE contribution rate or (ii) are no longer required to make CAYE contributions. Generally, the updated CAYE contribution rate will apply to service fees paid from the next day.
answer: Yes, excess CAYE contributions can be used to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years. However, any excess after that will be refunded to your bank account. You can also choose to retain excess CAYE contributions in your MediSave Account to earn up to 5% interest per annum and offset future MediSave payable. [Document 1]
